articleTitle: Submillimeter-scale Flexible Micro-catheters Driven by Shape Memory Alloys for Vascular Interventions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: A novel design of an active micro-catheter, as well as its fabrication and assembly processes, for active navigation in vascular interventions is proposed in this work. A prototype of such micro-catheters consisted of a silicone rubber catheter and the guide tip or actuator developed via embedding the U-shape SMA wires into the silicone rubber base. The U-shaped part of the SMA wire was detwinned to retain the residual strain for the performance of the guide actuator, and the demolding process was optimized by using a tensile device to obtain the guide actuator, followed by in-situ characterization using the infrared camera. Moreover, a catheter feeding mechanism enabling automatic control of such micro-catheters was proposed in the work, which could provide both axial and circumferential feed motions. A micro-clamp based on piezoelectric ceramic was then introduced into the mechanism to ensure stable clamping of the micro-catheter. The performance of the guide actuators was dominated by the residual stress and shape memory effects of the biased SMA wires. As a result, a bending angle of approximately 100° was realized by the guide actuator, suggesting its great potential for active and efficient navigation in narrow blood vessels.

articleTitle: Preparation of Bionic Anisotropic Superhydrophobic-Surface Based on Ti6Al4V Alloy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Ti6A14V alloy, as a promising metal material, is now widely used in many fields, such as aerospace, chemical and medical equipment, automotive engineering and so on. Providing better surface properties to Ti6A14V alloy has important research value. To achieve this goal, herein, the bionic super-hydrophobic surface inspired by indocalamus leaves with anisotropic wettability is fabricated on the surface of Ti6A14V alloy using nano-second laser followed by chemical modification. The protrusion, groove, and ridge like structures imitating the indocalamus leaves surface were achieved by twotime laser etching method. The surface morphology was observed by SEM, the wettability and anisotropy on the bionic super-hydrophobic surface were studied in detail. Meanwhile, we conducted a detailed analysis on the anisotropic wettability of the surface. We believe that this paper can provide theoretical significance and application expansion in improving the surface functionality of Ti6A14V alloys.

articleTitle: Galvanometer Based In-situ Imaging and Inspection System with Variable Ranges and Resolutions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In-situ measurement and inspection is essential for laser precision machining. This paper proposes a novel in-situ imaging system using a galvanometer scanner and a luminance sensor. The system operates by having the galvanometer scan the plane in a point-by-point manner, while the luminance sensor records the light intensity at each point. By organizing the recorded light intensities based on their corresponding positions, an image of the scanned plane is obtained. Compared with the existing in-situ imaging systems, the proposed one could realize variable imaging ranges and resolutions, and directly provides the image in the angle coordinates of galvanometers. Various experimental results demonstrate the imaging capability and the spatial resolution of the proposed system. Furthermore, a blind deblurring technique is employed to enhance the image quality. This system has the potential of achieving in-situ laser processing and inspection.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis for Triaxial Flexure Mechanisms with Symmetric Overconstrained Configurations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Compliant mechanisms have been wildly used in high-precision positioning stages of obtaining in-plane motion. In contrast, the study of multi-axis spatial motion stages shows a deficiency in recent years. In this work, a triaxial translational compliant mechanism design is proposed by employing diverse flexure elements and over-constrained symmetric configuration, which can support high-precision and spatial-decoupling positioning capability. A generalized theoretical model is established to incorporate those utilized flexure elements into a unified framework, and the analytical stiffness model of the triaxial compliant mechanism is also obtained through the compliance transformation matrix method. Furthermore, finite element analysis (FEA) is conducted to verify the analytical results and evaluate the over-constrained symmetric (OS) configuration compared with the nonsymmetric (NS) one. Finally, the characteristics of the stage with symmetric configuration are investigated through a key parameter study. The results show significant potentials in applications such as micro-nano laser direct writing which require multi-dimension and high-precision positioning and alignment of wafer stages.

articleTitle: Research Progress on Anti -tumour, Anti-microbial and Anti-viral Activities of Crocodile Blood
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The crocodile has important ecological, scientific and economic values, and it is of importance to study its medical functions such as anti-tumour, anti-microbial and anti-viral. The composition, function and application of crocodile blood are the focus of research at present. This article reviews the functional and active components of crocodile blood in terms of anti-tumour, anti-microbial and anti-viral activities, and its development prospects were introduced.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer-based Repetitive Control with Application to Fast Tool Servo System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: As the most potential precision manufacturing technology, the Fast Tool Servo (FTS) technology is widely employed to machine micro-nano structures. During the manufacturing process, the FTS system is commanded to track particularly periodic trajectory corresponding to the array arrangement of micro-nano structures. The tracking performance of the FTS system is full of challenge in presence of environmental vibrations, cutting-load variation as well as system parameter variations. By regarding these effects as the equivalent input disturbance, we propose a Disturbance Observer (DOB) based repetitive control structure for the piezo driven FTS system, such that the undesired amplification of non-periodic disturbances caused by the repetitive controller is compensated by the DOB. Considering the disturbance observe performance and robustness against of system uncertainties, the design of the DOB is transformed as an $\mathrm{H}\infty$ optimization problem. The developed control structure is finally implemented on the prototype of FTS system. Real time experimental results effectively verify tracking performance and disturbance rejection capability, as well as robustness against system uncertainties.

articleTitle: Study on Continuous Corrosion Process of Self-healing Coating with Micro-nano Capsule
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The continuous corrosion process plays an important role in the deterioration process of the coating, which reduces the shielding ability of the coating and enhances the electrochemical reaction of interfacial corrosion to accelerate the coating peeling. In this paper, the self-healing coating with micro-nano capsule is prepared based on the previous work. And the continuous corrosion process, surface roughness, and corrosion morphology are investigated. It will provide scientific research significance for the dynamic corrosion behavior.

articleTitle: Flexible AZO Thin Film Transistors Fabricated at Room Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Flexible thin film transistors (TFTs) were fabricated on polyimide (PI) substrate at room temperature (RT). The channel layer, which adopted aluminum doped zinc oxide (AZO) thin film, was deposited by the co-sputtering method with Al and ZnO as the targets. During the fabrication process, the radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering power of Al target was controlled to enhance the electrical performance of the AZO-TFTs. When the RF power of Al was 15 W, the device achieved the optimal on-off current ratio of $5.23 \times 10^{5}$.

articleTitle: Influence of Amorphous State Local Structure in Tinicu Alloys on Structure and Phase Transformations during Crystallization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The study of TiNiCu alloy samples in the initial state after quenching by EXAFS revealed the dependence of the local atomic structure of the alloys on the copper content. Studies of the structure of alloys by X-ray diffraction (XRD) using synchrotron radiation with a wavelength of 0.8 Å showed that in the initial state after quenching, the alloys are in an amorphous state. After isothermal crystallization of alloys at a temperature of 500° C for 300 s, it was found that samples of alloys with a copper content of more than 30 at.% after crystallization became so brittle that they were unsuitable for further research. This is a consequence of the peculiarities of the local atomic structure of the alloys identified by the EXAFS method. Temperature intervals and the nature of alloy phase martensitic transformations (MT) were determined by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC).

articleTitle: A Novel Cross-flow Wood Filter for Efficient Water Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Water resource shortages have been regarded as an important problem across the world, and membrane filtration technology is one of the effective measures. As a sustainable and renewable biomass material, natural wood owns a fine hierarchical three-dimensional interconnected microstructure that is composed of perpendicularly aligned microchannels lined with micropores. Micropores on the channel walls exhibit suitable rejection ability, providing an advantage to filter water while the treatment speed is severely limited. In this study, we demonstrated a cross-flow wood filter in which muddy water can be transferred along the microchannels and out of the vertically stacked micropores. The cross-flow wood filter takes full advantage of the micropores without sacrificing the speed of hydraulic flow within the main transport channels, exhibiting excellent performance for mud removal. In this manner, the treatment efficiency of turbidity, decolorization, and water flux is highly dependent on the groove number, depth, and thickness of the filter. At vacuum filtration, the turbidity removal rate and decolorization rate of an 8 mm-thick cross-flow wood filter with 3 grooves and 2 mm depth reached around 99% and 92% at a water flux up to 6.75 L/(m$^{\mathrm{2}}\cdot$ h), featuring a compromise between the mutually exclusive properties. The design of the cross-flow wood filter provides an available platform that can be extended to various wastewater treatment processes with different impurities, displaying a good application prospect in the wastewater treatment field.

articleTitle: Optimization and Experimental Study of The Cathode in Array Microchannel Copy Electrochemical Machining
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The processing quality of the array microchannels, as a critical component structure of the metal bipolar plates of fuel cells, has an important impact on the performance of fuel cells. Due to the high efficiency and quality of electrochemical machining (ECM), it is often used to process array microchannels. Traditional array microchannel electrochemical machining only considers factors such as stray corrosion or flow fields, while very little is optimized for the cathode. This paper set four cathode spacings (0.6 mm, 1.0 mm, 1.4 mm, 1.8 mm). The profile morphology of the array microchannels with different cathode spacings was compared by simulation combined with experiments. The cathode spacing of 1.4 mm was found to have the lowest stray corrosion intensity and the highest processing quality in the non-machined area of the microchannels.

articleTitle: A Study on the Multi-parameter Modulation of the Light Field in 4+1 Beam Laser Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study delves into the modulation of multiple parameters in the beam of a 4+1 beam laser interference lithography system. Simulations and analyses were executed from four aspects—initial phase, angle of incidence, azimuthal angle, and polarization—to understand the transformations in the two-dimensional/three-dimensional interference patterns post-modulation. Findings indicate that wave vector fundamentally determines the specific lattice structure of the interference light field. Although a four-beam setup can realize all 14 types of Bravais photonic crystals, laser interference involving more than four beams, which generates compound lattice structures, continues to possess remarkable value in material science and photonics

articleTitle: Applications of Graphene in NEVs Paves Paths to a Carbon-neutral Auto Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The global energy and climate environment are currently experiencing enormous challenges, and reducing carbon emissions has become an important goal for environmental protection in all countries. Many countries have made it a legislative obligation to reduce carbon emissions, and the most viable path to achieving carbon neutrality in the automotive and transportation sectors is the development of new energy vehicles (NEVs). NEVs will dominate automobile development in the future, and countries and regions such as China, Europe, the United States, and Japan have made comparatively excellent progress. However, the challenge of new energy vehicle development is mostly centered on storage and charging technologies and mileage anxiety. Graphene is ultra-thin, ultra-light, super-strong, and transparent, with high electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, light transmittance, mechanical properties, surface adsorption qualities, and other features. It has the potential for fast charging and enormous capacity storage, as well as ultra-light and ultra-durable materials, etc. It will boost the development and popularity of new energy vehicles if it has mature applications in energy storage materials, thermal management systems, body and parts materials, and so on. In this study, we investigate the applications and possibilities of graphene in new energy vehicles from the perspective of carbon neutrality in the automobile industry, in order to identify the most likely paths to carbon neutrality in the automotive sector by applying graphene.

articleTitle: Controlling DNA Capture by Electroosmotic Flow of Oppositely Charged Nanopores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: DNA sequencing technology based on nanopores has attracted wide attention in recent years, and graphene nanopore films with unique structure and properties have natural advantages in DNA sequencing. This powerful technology allows amplification-and label-free detection, which can be scaled up for high-throughput sequencing. In order to improve the efficiency of DNA sequencing in graphene nanopores, it is necessary to improve the ability of the nanopore to accurately capture DNA molecules. Here we designed a double-nanopore capture system to control the capture of DNA by a specific nanopore through positive and negative charges in the nanopore wall.

articleTitle: Effect of Argon-oxygen Ratio on the Performance of AZTO Thin Film Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, rare-element-free thin film transistors (AZTO-TFTs) were successfully fabricated with aluminum-zinc-tin oxide (AZTO) film preparing as the channel layer. The AZTO film was deposited by RF magnetron sputtering method. The effect of argon-oxygen ratio on the properties of AZTO thin films and electrical performance of AZTO-TFTs were studied. When the argon-oxygen ratio was 98:2, the transmittance of AZTO films could reach more than 90 % in the visible long-wave band, and the fabricated AZTOTFT exhibited excellent performance, including a field effect mobility $(\mu_{\mathrm{sat}})$ of $4.71\mathrm{~cm}^{2}/\mathrm{V}\cdot\mathrm{s}$, a subthreshold swing $(SS)$ of 0.37 $V/$ dec, a current on-to-off ratio $(\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{on}}/\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{off}})$ of $1.83\times 10^{8}$.

articleTitle: Structural Dynamics Analysis of Endebius Florensis’ Hindwing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Focusing on the dynamic characteristics of the hindwing structure of Endebius Florensis, a finite element model was established and analyzed to determine its modal characteristics, including natural frequencies and mode shapes. This analysis further explored the harmonic response and random vibration characteristics, examining the response of the hindwing structure under stable and random vibration loading. Finally, a transient dynamics analysis was carried out to investigate the response characteristics under time-varying loads. The first two modes had the highest effective mass ratio, and the predominant mode was up-down bending deformation. Under a fixed load of 0.03 N, the harmonic response produced total displacements and equivalent stress values of 50.6 mm and 1.5 GPa, and 24.52 mm and 0.61 GPa, respectively. The second bending cycle was similar to the previous one, but with a larger maximum displacement deformation. Under load, the displacement changed 1.74 mm compared to the initial position.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Study of C/SiC Composites by Laser-ultrasonic Hybrid Micromachining
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: High strength, high stiffness, low density, low thermal expansion coefficient, etc., are all characteristics of C/SiC composites, but fiber extraction, matrix cracks and burrs are prone to occur during processing which make it difficult for the parts to meet the requirements of high precision and quality. Laser-ultrasonic hybrid micromachining (L-UHM) is a recent research hotspot and has been shown to have a positive impact on the machining quality of ceramic matrix composites. The research focuses on L-UHM’s effects on the processing of C/SiC composites at various fiber orientations. Through the analysis of the temperature field simulation of laser parameters on the effect of heat affected zone (HAZ), and conventional machining (CM) and L-UHM orthogonal micromachining models were established to investigate how two alternative fiber direction cutting circumstances affect the failure mode of C/SiC composites. The findings indicate that compared with CM, LUHM significantly improves the surface quality both in the vertical longitudinal fiber direction and the parallel fiber direction. When $\mathrm{P}=60\mathrm{W}/\mathrm{m}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ and $\mathrm{A}=6\mu \mathrm{m}$, respectively, the surface roughness is reduced by 29.9 % and 35.3 %, respectively.

articleTitle: A Novel Stacked-graphene-line Printing Method Enabled by Droplet Ejection and Micro-pen Writing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Graphene emerged a broad application prospect in the field of electronics due to its atomically thin structure and fascinating conductivity properties. Miniaturization and integration are the roadmaps in electronics such as chips and multi-function sensors. However, the flexible and efficient printing technique of graphene patterns in the vertical direction is still challenging. In this work, we proposed a method to prepare stacked graphene patterns by droplet ejection and micro-pen writing techniques. The conductive graphene lines were printed by the droplet ejection, following by the micro-pen writing insulating cellulose nanotibril (CNF) line and the CNF film. Finally, a microstructure containing two-layer graphene lines was successfully prepared through alternating graphene lines and CNF films printing. Our work provides an accessible method for multi-layer graphene pattern printing, paving the way for the development of integrated electronics.

articleTitle: M/LDH-enhanced Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry for Metabolite Screening
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Herein, the surface-modified M/layered double hydroxides (LDHs) were demonstrated capable of analyzing small metabolites by laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI MS). We first synthesized the M/LDHs with a designed host-guest structure via a one-pot ultrasound method. Based on the high signal response and low background interference at a low mass range (< 1000 Da), the M/LDHs have a good performance in small metabolite detection using LDI MS. Therefore, the assay of M/LDH-enhanced LDI MS has broad prospects in applications for metabolite screening, biochemical analysis, and disease diagnosis, etc.

articleTitle: IR Cut-off Film of Target Microsttucture Surface Scattering Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: To assist to research on a microstructure scattering parameters, reflect 1064nm wavelength and make visible light through target surface, an infrared cutoff filter is proposed. In order to enhance the laser damage threshold and optimize the distribution of the temperature field, based on the parameters requirements and thin film electromagnetic field theory, and were used as coating materials, a merit function was built, and a film was designed in which the electric field intensity was lower and reflectivity was higher, through the simulated annealing algorithm. Electron beam heating evaporation and an ion-assisted deposition system were adopted in film preparation. By simulating curve, the functional monotonicity of the reflectivity was studied. It was determined that the ratio between high and low index material has an impact on the equivalent refractive index function and reflectivity. Through adjusting the high film sensitive thickness, the film mismatching issue was solved. The average transmittance between 380nm and 780nm was more than 97.2%, the average reflectance in 1150± 20nm was more than 99.99%, and the average reflectance in 1270± 20nm was more than 99.99%. It is shown that the infrared cutoff filter can meet the requirements of environmental testing, and has a high laser damage threshold.

articleTitle: Surface Modification of Co-Cr-Mo Alloy to Improve Antibacterial and Biocompatibility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This article uses laser direct writing to structurally process Co-Cr-Mo alloy, forming periodic microstructures then silver film is deposited on the structured surface to achieving a functional surface that combines antibacterial and biocompatibility. The antibacterial effects and cell proliferation were tested on silver-plated surfaces with different periodic structures of 20μm and 40μm. The results showed that the modified Co-Cr-M alloy had a 100% antibacterial rate on both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, and all samples exhibited excellent biocompatibility. The structured surface can promote cell proliferation and modulate cell growth morphology. This technique has great potential in addressing bacterial infections caused by medical implants.

articleTitle: Flow Field Analysis of Cylindrical Array Structurer in Electrochemical Machining Titanium Alloy Blades
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Titanium alloy has good stiffness and corrosion resistance. It has a wide range of applications in the aerospace industry. In electrochemical machining, high speed and uniform electrolyte flow are important to achieve a stable machining process. This paper presents a cylindrical array microstructure cathode. Different fluid models were established by changing the characteristic parameters of the array microstructure. And CFD software was used for numerical simulation. Numerical calculations show the electrolyte flow uniformity is best when spacing is 100 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ and arrangement is rectangular. Relevant ECM experiments were performed. Microstructure cathodes with all four parameters can achieve stable processing for at least 1500 s. The surface quality of the blade processed by the cathode with the optimal flow method obtained from the simulation result is the best, and reached 0.574 $\mu \mathrm{m}$. This paper's process methods apply to the extended manufacturing of difficult-to-process materials.

articleTitle: A Technique for Reducing the Velocity of Protein Translocation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Proteins are essential for the structure and function of cells and organs in living creatures. Several other biological activities, including controlling gene translation, interaction among cells, and the movement of molecules across cell membranes, depend on them as well. Due to their incredible resolution and great sensitivity, nanopores have been shown to be efficient tools for single-molecule biosensors; yet, the fast translocation velocity of protein molecules through them remains a substantial obstacle for protein sequencing. According to this research, the velocity of protein translocation through hybrid nanopores consisting of silicon nitride membranes and carbon nanotubes can be well controlled. The significant interaction between protein molecules and the surface of carbon nanotubes is responsible for this slowed motion. Moreover, different protein residues can be found to exhibit varying degrees of blocking currents by investigating the translocation of proteins containing various amino acids through hybrid nanopores. This effectively captures enough current signals to enable more precise protein sequencing.

articleTitle: Research on Classification and Recognition of Micro Milling Tool Wear Based on Improved DenseNet
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In order to detect the wear of micro-milling tools, proposing a deep learning neural network detection method based on improved DenseNet. Firstly, the Inception structure adds a multi-channel fusion of features. Secondly, the SE self-attention blocks are added. Finally, the whole network uses the pre-activation structure. The experiment results validate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The results show that the improved DenseNet can accurately identify and classify the 1 mm micro-milling tool wear state.

articleTitle: Influence of Crystallization Conditions on Local Atomic Structure of Austenite in Rapidly Quenched Tinicu Shape Memory Alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The local crystalline environment of Ni and Cu atoms in the quasi-binary TiNi-TiCu shape memory alloys containing 30 and 40 at.% Cu has been studied using EXAFS spectroscopy. Amorphous melt-spun alloy ribbons have been crystallized by isothermal annealing or by exposing to a short (10 ms) electric pulse. Analysis of the EXAFS spectra has shown that electropulse crystallization has a more noticeable effect on the local atomic structure of austenite compared to martensite. In particular, it leads to a decrease in the local disorder of atoms in the Cu coordination shells, a decrease in the lengths of Cu-Ni and Cu-Cu bonds, hinders an increase in the lattice parameter of the austenite phase and stabilizes its crystal structure. The observed changes in the local atomic structure of the austenite phase of the alloys contribute to the improvement in the shape memory properties.

articleTitle: Surface Nano-Structuring of Semiconductors by Nanosecond Pulsed Laser Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this work, we present an innovative approach for nano-structuring semiconductor surfaces using an in-situ patterning process. Nanosecond pulsed direct laser interference patterning (DLIP) combined with epitaxial growth is introduced to create functional surface features on semiconductors in a rapid single-exposure step. By utilising two to four laser beams, submicron periodic nanostructures including 1D nano-gratings, 2D nano-islands and nano-holes are fabricated, serving as nucleation centres for the formation of quantum dots. The ability to create periodic features offers control over the spatial arrangement and properties of the resulting quantum structures. This direct and efficient nature of the technique makes it promising for practical applications in various fields, such as optoelectronics, nanophotonics and quantum technologies.

articleTitle: A Morphology Control Method of Submicron SiO2 Arrays in CHF3/Ar Inductively Coupled Plasma Etching
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching is currently widely used for the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> etching process in the semiconductor device manufacturing industry. In this work, we studied the effect of process parameters on SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> films based on the CHF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/Ar gas mixture via ICP etching and obtained a good approach for controlling profile morphologies of submicron SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> arrays under a hard mask. According to the study, the expected structures can be successfully obtained by optimizing the recipes. The method developed in this work are scalable to large-volume sub-microstructures manufacturing.

articleTitle: Study of the Sensitivity of MAPbI3 Radiation Detectors Based on Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Perovskite radiation detectors have gained significant attention owing to their superior performance. In this study, we employed Geant4 Monte Carlo simulation to determine the detection sensitivity of MAPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> radiation detectors and identify the optimal physical conditions for achieving maximum detection sensitivity. It has been observed that the transport properties of materials with high atomic numbers significantly impact their detection sensitivity.

articleTitle: DNA Network Construction by Optically Induced Dielectrophoresis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this work, an optically induced dielectrophoretic force field was used in manipulating deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and a DNA network was formed at the position of virtual electrode which was observed by atomic force microscope (AFM). The amorphous hydrogenated silicon (a-Si:H) film was used to structure the virtual electrodes when a beam of light from a projector was illuminated into it and the illuminated area became conductive. The mica was used as the substrate of DNA and placed between the two ITO electrodes. An AC electric field of 2 V peakto-peak at 50 kHz was used across the electrodes. The mica substrate with DNA solution was naturally air dry after functioned with the optically induced dielectrophoresis (ODEP) force and scanned by AFM. The results show that DNA was attracted by positive dielectrophoretic force and converged at the position of virtual electrode, and the overall shape and the specific position of DNA network on substrate could be controlled by changing the virtual electrode shape and position. The average height of the DNA networks was close to the real height of DNA, which was helpful for analyzing the DNA network electrical conductivity. This work has proven that the ODEP can be used as the tool to manipulate DNA and structure DNA molecular devices.

articleTitle: Development of Nanostructures Based on Nanowires by Shape Memory Alloy Instruments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The article is devoted to solving urgent problems of nanotechnology and physics of nanostructures aimed at developing highly sensitive bionanosensors designed to solve difficult problems of diagnosing biological agents, in particular viruses. The high sensitivity of bionanosensors of biological molecules up to attomolar levels is achieved due to the fact that field-effect nanotransistors have a sensitive element in the form of a nanowire, the transverse size of which is comparable to the size of a bionanoagent, for example, a virus. Taking into account the fact that semiconductor nanowires are an extremely technologically advanced and cheap object, the wide application of such nanosensors based on field-effect transistors is hindered by the lack of only the technology for their manufacture. We have improved the technology of mechanical nanoassembly of structures such as field-effect transistors from suspended semiconductor nanowires. The selection of materials was carried out, and the technology for manufacturing nanostructures based on semiconductor nanowires was developed.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Superhydrophobic Hierarchical Structures on PET Surfaces by Hot Embossing with in Situ Growth of Silver Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach for achieving superhydrophobic properties on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) surfaces by combining hot embossing and in situ growth of silver nanoparticles (Ag NPs). The resulting surface features a hierarchical micro-nano composite structure, with micron-scale stripes overlaid by nanoscale bumps formed by Ag NPs. This structure exhibits high roughness as well as low surface energy, which contribute to its excellent superhydrophobicity. The contact angle (CA) of the surface can reach 162°, representing a significant improvement compared to smooth PET surfaces, with a 70% increase. Furthermore, the Ag NPs present on the surface offer additional functionalities, including electrical and thermal conductivity, optical properties and antibacterial properties. This research opens up new possibilities for fabricating superhydrophobic surfaces on thermoplastic materials like PET and expands the potential applications of PET in various fields.

Author Keywords: in situ growth of silver nanoparticles

articleTitle: Effect of Sputtered Oxygen Flux on Electrical Properties of Nanometer-thin indium-tin Oxide Transistors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In recent years, there has been significant attention directed towards field-effect transistors based on ultra-thin oxide semiconductors. In this study, we conducted an investigation into the electrical properties of ultrathin indium tin oxide (ITO) field-effect transistors under different oxygen partial pressures. Our experimental results reveal notable influences of oxygen flow rates on crucial transistor characteristics such as mobility, on/off ratio, and sub-threshold swing. Specifically, at an oxygen flow rate of 5 sccm, we achieved a high field-effect mobility (μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FE</inf>) of 58.9 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/V s, a threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</inf>) of -8.3 V, and a reasonable on/off current ratio (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>) of 4.4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. Moreover, to elucidate the vital role of oxygen in ultrathin ITO transistors, we utilized nitrogen as an alternative during the sputtering process. These findings provide valuable insights into the magnetron sputtering of nanometer-thin ITO field-effect transistors.

articleTitle: Research on High Precision Automatic Sample Loading Device for Blood Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: As the main steps of automatic blood analysis in vitro diagnostic instrument, sample extraction and loading play a key role in the whole sample preparation and result analysis. High speed preparation time and high loading accuracy are required in the preparation process of blood samples to be tested. In order to save the resting time of blood, improve the detection flux of the instrument and ensure the accuracy of data results, it is necessary to design an automated sample loading device with high precision and high speed. The sample loading device designed in this paper was composed of three parts including sampling module, robot arm system and turntable module, which directly carried out self-shaking, self-loading and incubation of blood samples in collecting vessels. The repeat alignment accuracy of the sample was $\leq\pm 50\mu \mathrm{m}$, and the loading speed was >200mm/s. The loading speed of the robot arm was >100mm/s. The accumulated error of the rotating disk was 80 $\iota\iota \mathrm{m}$, which realized the automatic preparation of blood samples with 50 $\mu$ and antibody reagents with 20 $\mu$. The testing result showed that the device fully meet the requirements of blood samples in the pre-treatment process of automated in vitro diagnostic instruments.

articleTitle: Realizing Micro-patterned Laser-reduced Graphene for Antiviral Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this work, graphene oxide (GO) was reduced by laser direct-writing (LDW) technology, a reduced graphene oxide (RGO) surface with micro-nano structures was fabricated by LDW. During the whole process, we can not only get pollution-free large areas RGO, but also control the RGO surface with micro-patterned grating structures. The antiviral performance against bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) of micro-patterned RGO surface compared to GO surface and petri dish were evaluated. The micro-patterned RGO exhibited excellent antiviral property which can be used in hospitals and public to prevent the spread of virus infections.

articleTitle: Formation of the Developed Surface of Dental Implants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper will highlight 6 possible methods for etching dental implants to create a developed surface and evaluate the results obtained by comparing the resulting surfaces with currently commercially available imported products.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Micro-volume Liquid Pipetting Device in Flow Cytometer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Flow cytometry is a kind of in vitro diagnostic instrument widely used for cell detection. Its sample pretreatment involves the marking, incubation, cleaning, mixing and other steps of antigen or antibody. Due to the inevitable human error and antibody loss phenomenon in the detection process, in order to reduce all kinds of waste caused by human error and improve the sample processing efficiency, it is an inevitable trend to introduce automatic sample pretreatment system which is depending on the precision and repeatability of micro-volume liquid pipetting device. The micro-volume liquid pipetting device designed in this paper is composed of manipulator control system, liquid path control and electric control system, within the pitetting range of 20$\mu 1-500\mu 1$, the accuracy is about $0.1\mu 1$, the coefficient of volume variation (CV) is less than 2%. The liquid level sensing has been improved for the application of flow detection of automatic micro-volume liquid pipetting.

articleTitle: Hollow Mo2C Nanofibers Improve the Electrochemical Performance of Cathode for Lithium-Sulfur Battery
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this study, convenient and rapid electrospinning technology is used to prepare molybdenum-carbide (Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C) loaded nanofibers and Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C loaded hollow nanofibers. The electrical conductivity of the sulfur cathode can be significantly improved through the utilization of Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C hollow carbon nanofibers as the supporting matrix material. Furthermore, the hollow nanofiber architecture can additionally function as a cushion to alleviate the volumetric alterations. Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C particles attached to the fiber surface can fully contact polysulfide and catalyze it to short-chain Li<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and Li<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The cathode electrode using hollow Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C nanofibers as matrix material exhibits an initial specific capacity of 904 mAh g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 0.2 °C. After 200 cycles, the composite cathode still maintain a reversible specific capacity of 573 mAh g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and capacity loss rate is only 0.18% per cycle. Hollow Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C nanofibers exhibit superior electrochemical performance compared to Mo<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>C nanofibers, thanks to the effective confinement of the shuttle effect and improved sulfur-utilization achieved through the construction of hollow structure. This work presents a straightforward and effective method for generating one-dimensional nanofibers as cathode support materials for lithium-sulfur batteries.

articleTitle: A method to Solve the Influence of Local High Temperature on Automatic Focusing of Infrared Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the development of photoelectric imaging, people’s requirements for machine vision are getting more ang more intelligence. In order to facilitate use, automatic focusing has become a popular research field. People from different directions, different dimensions, and different methods are used to analyze, obtaining a clarity evaluation function, and then focusing control. When high-temperature objects such as huge fire pits, tail flame of airplanes appear in the scene, based on the traditional SOBEL operator to calculate the grayscale gradient of images for automatic optical focusing, the infrared image response will be very large, and the grayscale will become very high, leading to the failure of the SOBEL operator and the failure of focusing. This article successfully solves the above problem by introducing grayscale average assistance.

articleTitle: Setup and Experiment for the Fusion of Molten and Solidified Micro-droplets in a Simulated Micro-gravity Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Uniform droplet-based manufacturing is promising in on-orbit metal additive manufacturing due to its advantages of no requiring specially prepared raw materials and delicate energy beam sources in printing process. However, the feasibility of the fusion among micro metal droplets in a micro-gravity environment ($\mu$G-MDF) should be first verified. To address this issue, a novel uniform droplets fusion setup was designed and established to test the fusion between uniform molten and solidified tin-lead droplets in free falling process. The fusion process was successfully recorded and droplet samples fused under simulated micro-gravity were obtained. The obtained samples demonstrated that the spherical droplets can be formed after impact and fusion. The morphology of the fused droplets was neat, illustrating that droplets can withstand larger collision speeds without splashing. A good fusion situation between molten and solidified droplets was achieved, laying the foundation for conducting uniform aluminum micro-droplets fusion experiments in the drop tube.

articleTitle: Feedforward and Feedback Combined Control of an XYΘ-Type Micro/nano Mechanism Using Multilayer Feedforward Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The hysteresis in piezoelectric actuator is one key element in affecting the motion precision of piezo-actuated systems. If combined with the system dynamics and kinematics, the influence of hysteresis will become even significant. For piezo-actuated mechanisms, a feedforward feedback combinatorial control method is proposed in this study. In the feedforward loop, a multilayer feedforward neural network (MFNN) is adopted as the feedforward hysteresis compensator. A PID controller is adopted in the feedback loop to account for the modeling uncertainties of MFNN and the external disturbances of the system. In this manner, the motion accuracy of the overall system can be improved. The effectiveness of the proposed method is experimentally tested on a piezo-actuated XYΘ-type mechanism. From the experimental results, it can be obtained that the maximum root-mean-square tracking errors of spiral and epicycloid trajectories are 44.0 nm and 84.4 nm, respectively. The results can demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits superior tracking performance in planar trajectories and achieves excellent hysteresis compensation performance for XYΘ-type micro/nano mechanism in tracking multi-DOF trajectories.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Monitoring of Intracellular Reactive Oxygen Species Based on Automated Nanoprobe Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The electrochemical detection of endogenous molecules from a single cell is a crucial technique for understanding fundamental cellular processes at the subcellular level and uncovering cellular heterogeneity. However, high throughput intracellular detection has posed significant challenges. This paper proposes a simple method for fabricating a nanoprobe for the electrochemical monitoring of intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), which are important signaling molecules that play a key role in a wide range of cellular processes, including apoptosis, proliferation, and differentiation. Combined with the automated nanoprobe platform, the study successfully achieved minimally invasive and efficient intracellular ROS detection in living cells. Moreover, the results reveal that the average ROS concentration in the cytoplasm and nucleus is uneven, which has important implications for the understanding of cellular redox signaling.

articleTitle: Multilevel Analog Modulation Based on Low Dimensional Optoelectronic Device Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The multilevel analog modulation unit is integrated by a dual-gate Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide transistor and Cadmium Selenide nanowire photodetector (1T1P). The transistor with dual-gate has reconfigurable transfer characteristic and resolved current output under different voltage application on dual gate, the nanowire photodetector has significantly favorable $5.55 \times 10^{15}$ Jones of specific detectivity and 5585.42 A/W of responsivity. The multilevel output in single integrated unit can be modulated in septenary by optical excitation that a detector is series with the top gate of transistor. The back gate of transistor also modulated quinary output under constant optical excitation.

articleTitle: Phase Imaging of Human Cells Using Digital Holographic Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Digital holographic microscopy (DHM) is a 3D method for imaging cells without using labels. It gives detailed information about cell shape and behavior. This study has explored two applications of 3D phase imaging. Firstly, an image was made of an out-of-focus mono chromatically illuminated cheek cell with a conventional light field microscope. The resulting Fresnel diffraction pattern associated with the cell images has been numerically refocused at various positions. The images show details of the organelles. the changing shape of the cell nucleus and the chromosomes within it. Secondly, a simple in-line DHM system used phase imaging to analyze cancer cells. The system uses a 532nm laser, 10x and 40x microscope lenses, and a CCD camera to achieve clear phase images with 250nm resolution and 23. 63x magnification. The system was used to view both the growth of cancer cells (SMMC-7721) and in a subsequent test the ability of fluorouracil, an anti-cancer drug, to destroy them. The DHM data displayed cell changes over at 24-hour intervals over a 24-96-hours period. Holographic Amplitude images show the shape of the cell and its nucleus, while phase images gave 3D cell structural details.

articleTitle: Pore-peptide Interaction Study of Polycationic-carried Amino Acid for Protein Sequencing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Nanopore sensors could measure electrical signals at the single-molecule level, which possess high sensitivity and selectivity. This characteristic has a broad application prospect in the field of protein sequencing. Biological nanopores have long blockade duration and a high blockade current ratio, which represents higher sensitivity for single molecule detection. However, considering the structural stability and sequencing chip industrialization, solid-state nanopore sequencing may be a long-term development direction in the future, which has been proved in the field of DNA sequencing. Here we simulated the detection of the single amino acid molecule under the traction of a polypeptide cationic carrier, based on silicon nitride nanopores. From the perspective of the potential distribution of nanopores, a more suitable type of traction amino acid was selected. In the steered molecular dynamics, we observed the periodic fluctuation of forces due to atomic scale contact. The specific fluctuation is similar to the fingerprint, which reflects the response of the nanopore to the amino acid. Combining the free energy landscape, differences in energy barriers were observed and provided a reasonable mechanical explanation corresponding to the pore-peptide interaction force. Our results demonstrate the mechanism of single amino acid recognition. These findings may pave the way to solid-state nanopore protein sequencing.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Thin-wall Structures with Femtosecond Laser and Stainless Steel Powder
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) has revolutionized the production of complex three-dimensional (3D) structures, but the fabrication of thin profiles with high precision and efficiency remains a challenge. This study explores the application of femtosecond laser-based additive manufacturing techniques for the production of thin profiles with micron-scale features. The study investigates the effects of scanning strategy, with optimized processing parameters, on the fabrication of thin profiles; the quality of the walls has been quantified by means of visual characterization of the melted volumes and the relation of the theoretical and measured thicknesses of the walls.

articleTitle: Metallic Black Color Obtained by Two Microstructures in Elytron Scales of Sagra Femorata Purpurea Lichtenstein
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Brilliant structural color has been widely explored in nature to obtain new technologies and methods conducive to the engineering. The metallic black appearance is a special existence compared to other purple, purple-red and green S. fp. Lichtenstein formed by microstructures. Here, the color formation mechanism of black elytra was investigated through microstructural observation, optical experiments and FDTD analysis. The reflectance of light gradually increases from 4% to 8% as the incidence angle adjusted from 0° to 60° with no peaks at the wavelength between 440 nm and 800 nm. According to the optical analysis of optical coupled bionic models, the circular convex closures have influence on angle dependent color changing light caused by irregular reflection and refraction while the incident angle less than 30°. The excessive thick layer in EPI can reflect and refract incident light absolutely irregular at different angles. It implies that the metallic black color of S. fp. Lichtenstein is achieved with the key factor of thick layer under the alternately distributed multilayers in EPI and the synergistic action of circular convex closures.

articleTitle: A Single-molecule Manipulation Instrument Integrated with in Situ Nanopore Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Nanopore sequencing is a powerful tool in the field of Genomics and Proteomics due to its long reads and identification of molecular modifications. However, there is still a challenge for locating a nanopore in manipulation-based sequencing with solid-state nanopore. In this paper, we developed an instrument for performing in situ nanopore fabrication and precise molecule manipulation in a seamless way. We successfully controlled a single λDNA molecule exiting a nanopore at a speed about 1 bp/s. The proof-of-utility of the instrument provides a strong support for the realization of solid-state nanopore-based sequencing.

articleTitle: The Structure and Optoelectronic Properties of Few-layer Phosphorus-implanted MoS2
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Due to its tunable bandgap, superior stability, natural surface passivation, and other unique properties, molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) has developed into the focus of research for new materials for photoelectric sensors. $M_{0}S_{2}$ is an inherently n-type, and phosphorus (P) implantation is proven to induce p-type doping, but there needs to be more study on the optoelectronic properties of $\mathbf{P}$ implanted $\mathbf{M}$ implanted with P dopants and annealed. In impact of P implantation on the structure and optoelectronic properties of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and the impact of annealing on the implantation effect, the pristine, the implanted, and the annealed samples are characterized and measured individually. Following P implantation, $M_{0}S_{2}$ evolves sulfur (S) vacancies, P impurities, and strained molecular structure, as evidenced by Raman spectra and XPS. P implantation created a p-type doping effect, increasing the response speed and decreasing the dark current through electrical and optoelectronic measurements. Subsequent investigations have found that annealing reduces S vacancies and P impurities in $M_{0}S_{2}$ and weakens the effect of P implantation on the structure and photoelectric properties of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. In conclusion, the research results of this paper provide a controllable p-type doping method for MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as well as the impact of this doping method on the photoelectric performance of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Copper Nanoparticle Antiviral Surface by Laser Direct Writing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The surface transmission of the virus can be divided into direct transmission and indirect transmission. With the outbreak of the COVID-19 epidemic, there is an urgent need for an antiviral surface that can effectively reduce surface contact transmission. In our work, a simple and efficient antiviral surface of copper nanoparticles was prepared by laser direct writing, which can effectively kill the virus, and the antiviral mechanism of Cu nanoparticles was discussed. The results indicate that the surface of the copper nanoparticles we prepared has efficient and good antiviral properties, which can effectively inactivate viruses in a short period of time, providing a way to prevent the spread of viruses through contact.

articleTitle: Design and Test of a Compliance Controller Based on the Piezoelectric-actuated Compliant Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: For grinding, polishing, and shaft-hole assembly tasks using industrial robots, flexibility demands during operation procedures of end-effectors increase rapidly. Unfortunately, current controllers are mainly focused on either the position or force, but rarely the force and position cooperation. This paper proposes a high-precision force-position cooperative compliance controller based on the compliant mechanism (CM). First, a piezoelectric-actuated CM was designed. Two force sensors and two position sensors were integrated. The statics and dynamics of the CM were analyzed and validated using the simulation. Second, the equivalent model of the piezoelectric-actuated CM was established. The force controller, position controller, and compliance controller were designed. Finally, the prototype system of the CM-based compliance controller was built. The statics and dynamics of the CM were tested. Indentation tests using three controllers were conducted. The microscope vision system and white light interferometer were employed to evaluate the performance. Prototype test results show that the CM-based compliance controller possesses a high force-position precision. The proposed CM-based compliance controller contributes to the force-position cooperative control of end-effectors of industrial robots.

articleTitle: Study of Single Point Incremental Sheet Metal Forming Trajectory Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Sheet metal single-point incremental forming technology is a fast and flexible sheet metal forming technology. The technology has great potential in multi-species, small-batch and highly flexible production. The use of contour-forming trajectory single-point incremental forming of complex-shaped parts is prone to problems such as local depression and material build-up, which seriously affects the forming performance of the product. In this paper, the relationship between forming angle and incremental arc length was established and the generation of contour trajectories was controlled based on ellipsoidal section part shapes. By using ABAQUS software, the effects of three different forming trajectories on forming quality, forming thickness, and contour variation were simulated and analyzed. The results show that the overall forming quality of the contour trajectories with equal arc lengths based on the dispersion of the lower pressure point is better, the difference between the contour of the numerically simulated model and that of the theoretical model is minimised and the overall thinning is minimised.

articleTitle: The Improvement of the Mechanical Exfoliation Method to Prepare Impurity-free Few-layer MoS2
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Mechanical exfoliation is the simplest and fastest way to produce Molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) materials with highly crystalline and atomic thin. Traditional mechanical exfoliation methods typically use 3M-Scotch tape (3M ST) and polydimethylsiloxane film (PDMS). However, the 3M ST often leaves residue on the material surface, and using acetone to remove the residue can introduce complications. And PDMS usually obtains materials with smaller sizes. In this study, we propose a new process based on traditional mechanical exfoliation methods, which involves the transfer of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to the substrate using a polyethylene protective film (PE) and 3M ST. Compared with the methods involving 3M ST and PDMS, the proposed method prepares MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> with larger size, thinner thickness, and completely eliminates residue. In addition, the obtained MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> shows excellent Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) effect with a detection limit of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> M for R6G, demonstrating the great potential of mechanical stripping technology in optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Manipulating Nanoscale Drilling Machines Based on Nested Carbon Nanotubes through Coding Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In recent years, micro/nano robots have been increasingly widely used, providing a strong guarantee for human health and safety, with micro/nano drilling machines being the most typical example. However, at present, it is difficult for people to accurately and effectively control micro/nano drilling machines without damaging the human body. Based on this, this paper designed a nanoscale drilling machine with adjustable charge based on nested carbon nanotubes. By simply using a pre-designed coding strategy, it is possible to control the charge density and position on the surface of the outer carbon nanotube, thereby controlling the rotation speed and direction of the nanoscale drilling machine, to achieve different goals. The driving force of the nanoscale drilling machine is provided by electrostatic force, and the drilling machine will slowly stop under the Van der Waals force between the inner and outer nested nanotubes. This device contributes to the realization of the prospect of “precision medicine”.

articleTitle: Application Research on Multi-dimensional Protection of Gas Pipeline against Corrosion
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The gas in the steel plant and power plant contains a large amount of acidic and corrosive gas, which is very likely to cause pipeline perforation, cracking and gas leakage, resulting in fire, explosion and personal injury and other malignant accidents, bringing significant losses to life and property and national economic construction. The problem of gas pipeline corrosion has become a major scientific and technical problem facing the gas pipeline. In view of gas pipeline corrosion problem, multi- dimensional protective measures such as gas pipeline and attached equipment materials gas pretreatment, new organic anti- corrosion materials and anodic protection for different parts and working conditions are systematically researched in order to achieve the overall protective effect.

articleTitle: Distinguishing Single and Double Stranded DNA Based on Solid State Nanopores
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Early diagnosis of diseases requires specific detection of certain biological molecules. Here, we propose a solid-state nanopore platform based on silicon nitride, which can detect and distinguish ssDNA (22 nt) and dsDNA (22 bp). Experimental data shows that the translocation of ssDNA and dsDNA in nanopores is controlled by competition between electro-osmosis and electrophoresis. At a pore size of approximately 10 nm, ssDNA is driven by electro-osmosis through the nanopores, while dsDNA is driven by electrophoretic forces through the nanopores. The current blocking caused indicates that the current blocking amplitude caused by dsDNA passing through the nanopores is twice that of ssDNA.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Large-stroke High-precision Compliant Attitude Regulator For MicroLED Laser Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In the process of laser mass transfer of MicroLED chips (size about $10 \sim 50 \mu \mathrm{m}$), extremely strict requirements are put forward for the alignment accuracy $(\lt \pm 500 \mathrm{~nm})$ between the chip carrier and the target substrate. Otherwise, the parallelism deviation and angle deviation between the chip solder joint and the target substrate will directly affect the product quality. To this problem, a large-stroke high-precision spatial attitude regulator based on flexure is proposed. Innovatively design a lever-bridge hybrid displacement amplification mechanism (LBDAM) with large displacement amplification ratio and high positioning accuracy. Static modeling and finite element analysis were carried out. Finally, an experimental system of spatial attitude regulator is established, and a closed-loop decoupling controller is built by kinematic inverse solution method and PID control method for the multiple-input multipleoutput coupling system. The performance tests of the motion travel and closed-loop positioning accuracy are carried out. The various experimental results indicate that the Z-stroke of the designed spatial attitude regulator can reach $250 \mu \mathrm{m}$, the closedloop repeated positioning accuracy is $\pm 100 \mathrm{~nm}$, and the closedloop deflection adjustment accuracy can keep within $\pm 2 \mu \mathrm{rad}$, which can realize precise adjustment of spatial attitude.

articleTitle: A New Simulation Method for 3-D Electron Beam Lithography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Electron beam lithography (EBL) is a micro processing technology that plays an important role in both semiconductor and nanotechnology fields. On the basis of a series of physical theories and models proposed by predecessors, this paper establishes models for electron scattering in solids and energy deposition models. The Monte Carlo method is used and corresponding development patterns are simulated through computer programming. The relationship between these patterns and factors such as incident electron beam energy, resist thickness, and incident dose are analyzed. Finally, the corresponding conclusion of improving resolution is obtained and compared through experiments, verifying the reliability of the model.

articleTitle: Research Progress of Immune Cells Against Tumor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The traditional treatment of tumors usually ignores the anti-tumor mechanism of the body’s own immune system. With the rapid development of immunology and tumor biology, tumor immunotherapy has become a research hotspot in recent years. Among them, anti-tumor immune cells have become a new effective means. In this paper, the key immune cells in the process of anti-tumor and their immune research progress are introduced, aiming at providing reference for tumor treatment.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Q-band Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: A compact and low noise amplifier (LNA) was designed and fabricated, by using state of the art micro-assembly technique. The circuit EM design, optimization and analysis were realized in AWR Microwave Office and Ansoft HFSS. The bonding wire based micro-assembly adjustment method was obtained to achieve a low noise performance. The fabricated LNA was based on a three stage structure, and was under a working range from 38GHz to 42GHz, with an associated gain of 55dB and noise figure as low as 3. 0dB. The final product size was only 59mm$\times$ 28.5mm$\times$ 28.5mm.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Optimization of Single Nanowire Optoelectronic Devices Based on Atomic Force Microscope
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: 1D photodetectors have attracted widespread attention because of their superior properties, however, the controlled fabrication and optimization of 1D photodetectors are still demanded. We reported a method of using AFM probe to fabricate nanowire photodetector as well as increase the contact between nanowires and metal electrodes through mechanical force applying. We used atomic force microscopy (AFM) to precisely move ZnO nanowires across electrodes to form photodetectors with an alignment resolution down to 100 nm. In addition, to increase the electrical contact of ZnO nan- owires and metal electrodes, we exerted force via AFM probe precisely on the nanowires. Results showed that the dark cur- rent of single ZnO NW increased by an order of magnitude from 45 nA to 500 nA. Finally, we further applied this AFM technique to construct a graphene/single ZnO nanowire/gra- phene photodetector. The fabrication process based on AFM involves minimal damage and contamination to the nanowire. And the mechanical force exerted by the AFM probe can en- hance the quality of the contact between the nanowires and the electrodes and improve the optoelectronic properties of the device.

articleTitle: Study on the Removal Mode of Ultra-Precision Polishing Process of Ceramic Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Ceramic is an important material of the optical components of the space reflective optical system. It is the great significance of obtain the space optical components with high quality and characteristics, and to study the ultra-precision polishing process of the ceramic surface. The computer control ultra-precision polishing ultra-precision flexible airbag polishing technology is used to study the optical surface polishing characteristics of silicon carbide material. Using the Taguchi method, the main parameters of polishing angle, rotation speed, pressure and compensation depth are studied to determine the optimal process parameters of ultra-precision polishing of ceramic surface.

articleTitle: Application of Optimization Algorithm in Meniscus-Constrained Electrodeposition of Three-Dimensional Metal Microstructure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Precision metallic micro-nano structures fabricated cost-effective by meniscus-confined electrodeposition (MCED) have potential applications in sensors and electronic devices. The tuning of deposition quality and deposition rate is of great importance for the MCED of micro-nano structured devices. Currently, accurately predicting the combination of process parameters during deposition is an effective way to regulate the quality and rate of deposited structures. Therefore, in this study, the process parameters of the MCED are analyzed and data sources are obtained through simulation, and the MCED process parameters are optimized by optimization algorithm to obtain high-performance metal microstructures. In addition, experiments with the optimized parameters on MCED equipment were performed with a maximum error of 7.1% relative to the target value electrochemical deposition rate. The processing of process parameters by optimization algorithms can regulate the quality and speed of deposited metal microstructures, and the results of the study are essential guidance for the actual deposition.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Ultrasonic Assisted Helical Grinding of Sic/Sic Composites
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the gradual improvement of the speed of aircraft and automobiles, in order to ensure their safe braking, the requirements for new brake materials and the demand for processing methods are becoming more and more urgent. SiC/SiC composites have drawn a lot of interest because of their exceptional qualities, including high strength, high thermal stability, and low density. The goal of this study is to compare traditional helical grinding (CHG) with ultrasonic vibration aided helical grinding (UVAHG). The ABAQUS finite element simulation model of single abrasive cutting of UVAHG and CHG was established to analyze the stress distribution on the material under different processing methods. It can be seen from the experimental results that the effect of ultrasonic vibration can significantly improve the stress concentration and crack propagation defects during the machining process of the workpiece, and the surface quality of the machined surface has also been improved.

articleTitle: Performance Study of 266nm UV Nanosecond Laser Micromachined Glow Discharge Polymer Films
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Glow discharge polymer (GDP) is the target of choice for ICF ignition due to its low density, dense structure, absence of grain boundary defects, infrared transparency and high surface finish, which can effectively reduce the initial perturbation of the implosion process and thus suppress RT instability during ICF implosion. In the process of ignition, in order to ensure that the energy of the ignition laser can be deposited near the compressed fuel core, specific microstructures need to be machined on the surface of the target pellet and relatively high requirements are placed on the surface quality of these microstructures. In recent years, laser ablation techniques have been widely used for the micro and nano processing of polymers due to their ability to produce precise microstructures. In this paper, laser processing experiments were conducted on GDP materials, and the processed surfaces were observed using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Variations in processing parameters were used to obtain the effect of laser ablation on the surface morphology of GDP materials. With an increase in laser energy density, the surface quality of the GDP material decreased, and the heat-affected zone became larger.As the scanning speed increases, the surface quality of the GDP material improves and the heat-affected zone becomes smaller.
