As the number of scans increases, the surface quality of the GDP material can be maintained at lower scan rates, and then starts to decrease as the number of scans increases further.

articleTitle: Laser-induced Zinc Metal Battery Anodes with Ultra-long Cycling Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Zinc ion batteries show great potential as favorable options for both portable and grid-scale applications due to their inherently high safety, low cost, and relatively high theoretical energy density. However, the flat zinc metal anodes are not capable of long cycling performance owing to severe dendrites formation during the charge-discharge process. In this study, we employed nanosecond laser to modify zinc surface morphology and surface chemistry in order to alleviate the dendrites growth. The results demonstrate that the laser-induced zinc foil (LZF) surfaces show super-hydrophilic property with microstructures and a layer of ZnO coating. The symmetric cells and half-cells investigations indicate that the LZF electrode possesses lower nucleation overpotential and stable plating/striping behavior. Moreover, excellent zinc ion battery performance is achieved with activated carbon (AC) cathode, stably working for 20000 cycles at 2 A/g and 50000 cycles at 10 A/g with the Coulombic efficiency almost 100%. This paper offers new option for laser fabrication of high-performance zinc anodes for Zn-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Electrospun Anisotropic Photoconductivitymagnetic-fluorescent Switch-typed 3D or 3D Plus 2D Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: New three-dimensional (3D) and 3D plus two- dimensional (2D) structures with anisotropic photoconductivity, magnetism, and fluorescence are prepared. Firstly, a switch-typed anisotropic photo-conductive Janus film (S-JF) is prepared by electrospinning, and the target structures are obtained by rolling 2DS-JF using different rolling strategies. Using [high concentration DF(H-DF)/polyvinyl pyrrolidone (PVP)]/polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)//[PVDF/Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/PVP] Janus nanofibers and [low concentration DF(L-DF)/polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)] nanobelts as construction units, the top and bottom layers of S- JF are constructed, respectively. In the absence of light irradiation, the 3D and 3D plus 2D structures only exhibit magnetism. Under ultraviolet light irradiation, due to the photo-conductive effect of DF, the sample conducts electricity along the direction in which the Janus nanofibers are arranged, and due to the introduction of the insulating part into Janus nanofibers, it is insulated in the perpendicular direction to the Janus nanofibers, resulting in conductivity anisotropy of the sample. At the same time, the two layers of S-JF have different fluorescence colors. Therefore, under light stimulation, the 3D and 3D plus 2D structures exhibit three properties: fluorescence, anisotropic conductivity and magnetism, which means that 3D and 3D plus 2D structures achieve the transition from single function to triple function through no light irradiation to light irradiation.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Superhydrophobic Carbon Fiber via Laser Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper proposes a method of fabricating micro/nanostructures on stainless steel surfaces using direct laser interference lithography, followed by template hot pressing. This method leaves micro/nanometric structures on carbon fibers, which, after treatment with fluorosilane, can construct robust carbon fibers with excellent mechanical properties and superhydrophobic performance on a stainless steel substrate. The novelty of this method lies in the simplicity of the preparation process and the powerful superhydrophobic capability of the carbon fibers, which can be produced on a large scale. This solves the issues of high preparation costs, complex processes, inherent performance degradation, and difficulties in mass production inherent in traditional fabrication techniques. The results demonstrate that the superhydrophobic capability of the carbon fibers prepared using this method is significantly improved compared to untreated surfaces, with contact angles reaching up to 164°

articleTitle: Localized Electrochemical Deposition for Additive Manufacturing of 3D Array Metal Microstructures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the recent rapid development of precision manufacturing and microelectronics, the fabrication of 3D array metal microstructures is a crucial and challenging problem in manufacturing. Based on the principle of reduced deposition of metal ions, the localized electrochemical deposition additive manufacturing technique has distinct advantages in the fabrication of metal microstructures, and its low cost facilitates a wide range of applications. This study used the micro-additive manufacturing technique of localized electrochemical deposition (LECD-μAM) to investigate the influence of extrusion pressure driving electrolyte solution flow on deposition results by simulation and experiment. Subsequently, a deposition body with a flat and smooth surface was realized based on pressure regulation. Sediments produced by this technique are of superior purity, containing up to 99.5% copper. At the same time, this technique has the advantage of low environmental dependence and high surface quality. It enables the additive manufacturing of complex 3D array metal microstructures at micron and submicron scales by localized electrochemical deposition. With the advantages of simple preparation, low cost, short preparation cycle, and controllable structure, this approach has a wide range of promising applications in various fields with significant potential.

articleTitle: Effect of Anion Hydration Lubrication at Negatively Charged Interface
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Numerous experiments and simulations have supported the impact of cations’ ability to hydrate on super-lubrication. The hydrated lubricating ability of anions is gradually attracting attention. Some scholars found that the anionic hydration layer near oppositely charged interface became less effective in lubrication as the concentration increased, inspiring us to start exploring the lubricating effect of the hydration ability of anions at the interface with similar charges. The findings demonstrate that anion hydration also contributes to the decrease in friction, and the impact of hydration lubrication is not positively correlated with salt solution concentration. The results of this experiment have a certain reference value for drag reduction and lubrication of fluid transport at micro and nano scale.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method for Digital Holographic Autofocusing of Micro Milling Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The sharpness evaluation of the digital holographic reconstructed image is the key problem of holographic auto-focusing. This paper proposes a sharpness evaluation method for digital holographic auto-focusing of micro-diameter milling tools, and the focusing process is divided into coarse focusing and fine focusing. In coarse focusing, the search step of the reconstructed distance calculation is in millimeter level, and the edge of the reconstructed image will have obvious oscillation, which cannot be accurately judged by the traditional sharpness evaluation function, but the amplitude of the wavelet transform high frequency coefficient of the most clearly focused image in the focusing window is the largest, and the sharpness evaluation of the reconstructed image can be accurately performed by using this characteristic. When fine focusing, the search step of the calculation of the reconduction distance is adjusted to micron level, and by obtaining the evaluation results of different evaluation functions, it is found that different evaluation functions can be evaluated accurately.

articleTitle: The Study of Electro-mechanical Phenomena in Single CNTs in the Cold Field Emission Scheme Using Nanomanipulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are one of the most interesting nanotechnological materials with many unique physical and functional properties. The uniqueness of many properties is manifested both in macro-samples containing CNTs and at the nano-level, in the case of single nanotubes. One of outstanding properties of CNTs, which manifest themselves both in macro-samples and in the case of single CNTs, is cold field emission. Another interesting property of CNTs is luminescence. By themselves, single nanotubes have unique mechanical, electrical, and electromechanical properties, and a single CNT itself can be considered as a subminiature nanó-electromechanical system (NEMS). Also, electromechanical phenomena and luminescence can occur in CNTs under conditions of cold field emission. The paper reports on the observation of electromechanical vibrations and optical emission from single carbon nanotubes in the cold field emission mode from a single nanotube.

articleTitle: Nanomechanical Oscillating Multi-Purpose Device Based on Alloy with Shape Memory Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: We propose and create a new nanomechanical oscillating device based on the shape memory effect of Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NiCu alloy. The device is designed for cutting and detaching micro- and nano-objects using its oscillating sharp tip. The oscillations have a frequency of up to 8 kHz and an amplitude of 1.2 μm. We performed an initial experiment to cut a ZiO nanowire using the new device. A numerical model of the device was developed to estimate the thermal activation frequency and mechanical resonant frequency based on its geometric parameters.

articleTitle: Research on the Distribution of the Circulation of Double-sided Polishing Method Based on Processing Forecast Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: For non-confirmed processing for the ring pendulum double-sided polishing (RPDP), this article constructs a machining prediction model based on the motion principle and pressure distribution principle of the RPDP equipment, and conducts simulation experiments using the machining prediction model as a platform It was found that the instantaneous material reduction is mainly distributed within the radius range of the pendulum grinding disc at the center of the component. The distribution of the large instantaneous material reduction band does not exceed the radius range of the pendulum grinding disc at the center of the component, and is independent of changes in the size and swing mode of the pendulum grinding disc. The large instantaneous material reduction band contracts inward as the swing interval of the pendulum grinding disc moves outward. Based on this law, this article guides practical processing by cupper the surface profile of optical components from $2.27 \lambda(\lambda=632.8 \mathrm{~nm})$ reduced to $1.85 \lambda$, and the obtained processing rules can effectively guide actual processing.

articleTitle: Analysis of Aerodynamic Characteristics of Bionic Flapping Wing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The bionic flapping wing micro air vehicle (FWMAV) has been widely studied due to its excellent aerodynamic characteristics. In this paper, learn from the beetle, Oides decempunctata Billberg, the bionic flapping wing (Bio- FW) was designed. In following, the effects of frequency and Angle of attack on its aerodynamic characteristics are studied by the obtained lift coefficient, drag coefficient and lift-drag ratio curves. The optimal aerodynamic parameters were obtained, and the pressure cloud diagram of the flow field and modification of the lift-drag ratio during a unit period were analyzed.

articleTitle: Protein Identification through a Graphene Nanopore Powered by Electroosmosis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Research on protein sequencing technology is a crucial topic in life sciences and medicine subjects. Accurate protein sequencing plays a crucial role in enabling disease treatment at the nanoscale. Graphene membrane with a nanopore is considered to be an effective single molecule sensing. Peptides translocation through a nanopore has been proved to be an effective tool for protein sequencing. However, challenges remain for unfolding peptides successfully translocation through a nanopore. By using Molecular Dynamic (MD) simulations, it is showed that electroosmosis is the main driving force for the peptide translocation. In addition, due to the electroosmotic effect, different amino acids pass through the nanopore with different blocking currents, which makes it possible to distinguish between different species of amino acids using nanopore sequencing methods. In this work, translocation of peptides through the graphene nanopore is achieved driven by electroosmotic flow, which can facilitate accurate amino acids (AAs) recognition and identification.

articleTitle: Study on Wear Evaluation of Cemented Carbide Micro Milling Cutter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: At present, as a micro-machining technology, micro-milling has a high demand in the fields of machinery, aviation and aerospace. Whether in the macro or micro milling process, tool wear will inevitably occur, and tool wear has a great influence on the machining efficiency and machining accuracy of the product. Therefore, it is of great significance to select the correct tool wear evaluation index for the study of tool wear in the production process. Because there is no standard blunt standard for micro-milling cutters, this paper explores the blunt standard of cutting tools through the milling test of micromilling cutters with a diameter of $\emptyset$ lmm and the selection of corresponding wear evaluation indicators.

articleTitle: A Large-area Nanograting as SERS Substrate by Displacement Talbot Lithography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper proposes a fabrication strategy based on displacement talbot lithography to realize nanograting on large-area, which achieves the fabrication of periodic nanostructure with low-cost, high resolution, and high uniformity. In addition, a layer of gold film was vapor-deposited on the top of the grating by physical vapor deposition technology for Raman spectroscopy detection. The obtained gold nanograting has a good Raman spectral signal enhancement effect, which is a repeatable, mass-producible SERS substrate in the new fabrication method.

articleTitle: Martensitic Phase Transition in TiNi Thin Plates with Different Surface Crystallographic Orientations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Atomistic simulations of monocrystalline TiNi thin plates with different crystallographic orientations were performed based on the classical molecular dynamics in the framework of Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS) package. It was found that the crystallographic orientation of the surface in a monocrystal plate has a significant effect on the phase transition temperature at nanoscale thickness. We have studied the surface energy dependence on temperature for surface crystallographic orientations (100), (110), (111), (112), (122). The stability of utilized model used was also investigated, which allowed us to conclude its satisfiability for these calculations.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic Performance of Bio-inspired 3D Corrugated Wings Learned from the Ladybird BeetleHindwing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Beetle hindwings have two specific features: the deployable hindwing and corrugation wing. In the low Reynolds numbers environment, the corrugated wing structure of insect wings proves to be essential for improving aerodynamics.In order to explore further whether flexible corrugated structure has a significant effect on aerodynamic effects. Two 3D corrugated wing models (3D-CW models) were designed with rigid and flexible properties, respectively. In this paper, based on ANSYS Fluent, the fluid-structure interaction method is used to solve the Navier-Stokes equations numerically. At a series of angles of attack, the flexible wing has better aerodynamics at angles of attack larger than 10°; the deformed leading edge can induce a stronger Leading edge vortex (LEV) than found at the rigid wing.

articleTitle: Study on Multifunctional MOF Nano Drugs Toxicity for Targeted Diagnosis and Treatment of Colorectal Cancer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Colorectal cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors. The chemotherapy drug doxorubicin (DOX) has been extensively used in cancer treatment, but its clinical toxicity has limited its application. Here, we report a multifunctional metal-organic framework (ZIF-8, Zn MOF) loaded with chemotherapy drugs (doxorubicin; DOX) and targeting peptides. The morphology and size of ZIF-8@DOX-Ti were studied by scanning electron microscopy. The DOX encapsulation rate of ZIF-8@DOX-Ti was $42.465 \%$ and the drug loading rate was $30.575 \%$. The results of MTT assay showed that ZIF-8@DOX@Ti had almost no toxic effect on normal cells, and had obvious inhibitory effect on SW480. ZIF8@DOX-Ti has the advantage of non-toxic and high drug loading, suggesting that it has the potential to deal with colorectal cancer.

articleTitle: Preparation of Micro Gripper Pincer End with Bionic Superhydrophobic Surface and Analysis of Gripping Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In recent years, micro grippers have been widely used in the micro/nanomanufacturing industry. However, during their application, the end face of the micro gripper pincer tends to adsorb impurities, making it difficult to release small objects during the gripping process, which affects their processing efficiency. To overcome these drawbacks and improve the performance of micro grippers, this study utilizes laser ablation micro/nano composite structures combined with fluorosilane chemical modification to rapidly prepare superhydrophobic surfaces with special wetting properties at the end of the micro gripper pincer, and the water contact angle (WCAs) at the pincer body reaches 156. 2 ± 2.0°, and the rolling angle (RAs) reaches 2. 2 ± 0.6°. The surface of this type of micro gripper effectively suppresses the adsorption of impurities at the gripping end and enhances the release performance of the gripper for microparticles. Additionally, this study systematically investigates the formation mechanism of the superhydrophobic surface on the pincer end of micro gripper by the analysis of three-dimensional surface topography and surface chemical composition, providing a foundation for the rapid preparation of superhydrophobic functional surfaces on gripper ends.

articleTitle: Design of a Flexure Mechanism Based on ETC Type Two-axis Flexure Hinges for Nano-positioning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Two-axis flexure hinges play a pivotal role in the design of spatial flexure-based mechanisms for nano-positioning. In this study, we have undertaken the development of an asymmetric XYZ translational nano-positioning stage, incorporating a novel type of flexure hinges characterized by elliptical transverse cross-sections (ETC). The structure design of both the flexure hinge and the flexure mechanism is outlined. Furthermore, the motion characteristics of the flexure mechanism are investigated and compared with a flexure mechanism of identical configuration, but utilizing traditional flexure hinges with rectangular transverse cross-sections (RTC). Our findings reveal that substituting the RTC type flexure hinges with the ETC type ones has minimal impact on the motion transfer of the flexure mechanism with an identical configuration. However, under identical displacement actuation, the ETC-type flexure hinges exhibit reduced stress concentration, resulting in lower maximum stresses within the mechanism. Additionally, the ETC-type flexure hinges demonstrate increased compliances, leading to decreased actuating forces and indicating a higher level of transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Cu-doping Micro-Nano Grooved Structures on Ti6Al4V Alloy by Laser Direct Writing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In this paper, the micro-nano grooved structures with a period of 70um were prepared on the surface of Ti6A14V allowy by fiber laser direct writing technology, and Cu was doped on the grooves by ion sputtering and annealing processes. The effects of laser power and scanning speed on the topography and feature size of grooved structures on Ti6A14V allowy surface were studied. The topography was characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results showed that the micro-nano grooved structures were formed when the laser power was 12W and the scanning speed was 10mm/s. The effect of Cu doping on micro-nano grooved structures was studied by adjusting the Cu doping from 1% to 50.7% by ion sputtering. The results of elemental analysis (EDS) showed that the nanostructures were generated on the micro grooved structures when the Cu-doped content was 19.1%.

articleTitle: TA@Au Nanoflower-assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Mass Spectrometry for Metabolite Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Novel tannic acid functionalized gold nanoflowers (TA@AuNFs) based laser desorption and ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) has been introduced for the analysis of small molecule metabolites. TA@AuNFs were synthesized using a one-pot green method and were demonstrated as an excellent LDI-MS matrix in metabolic analysis. Subsequently, our proposed method was utilized in metabolic profiling of complex biological samples such as serum, urine, cerebrospinal fluid, and prostatic fluid, with high signal intensity $(\sim10^{5})$. This research shows promising prospects in the analysis of clinical metabolites and disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Technology for Obtaining Membranes Based on Porous Silicon
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: A technique has been developed and tested for obtaining membranes based on porous silicon structures with a different pore morphology (such as nanostructured silicon, macrostructured silicon, and structures with gradient porous layers with a variable morphology (GPSi-var)). The influence of mechanical stresses on the destruction of membranes during mechanical processing was studied. The technology allows to create membranes based on a porous silicon structure with low mechanical stresses which can be used in various filtering devices with modifying characteristics of the porous layer depth and the pore diameter.

articleTitle: Mesoporous Platinum Nanospheres for Sensitive Detection of Small Metabolites by Mass Spectrometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Sensitive metabolite detection in biofluids is crucial in in-vitro detection and commonly relies on the designed materials-based platform. However, metabolic analysis in biofluids is hindered by laborious sample pretreatment due to its complexity and sample abundance. Herein, we construct a mesoporous platinum (Pt) nanospheres system to enhance the laser desorption/ionization process for sensitive metabolites analysis. We successfully synthesize porous Pt nanoparticles with tunable surface structure by a simple surfactant-direction method. The nanoparticles promote the laser desorption/ionization process, demonstrating its sensitivity to standard metabolites (with a limit of detection down to 1.74 pmol, 100 times higher than traditional organic matrices). Notably, our platform directly realizes the sensitive detection of metabolites in biofluids (serum, plasma, urine, and cerebrospinal fluid) without sample pretreatment due to the size-selective effect of the porous structure. Our work will contribute to advancing techniques for metabolic analysis and developing novel materials-based platforms for in-vitro diagnostics.

articleTitle: Treatment of Carbon Nanotube Thread in a Microwave Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The effect of a high-power microwave magnetic field on carbon nanotube (CNT) thread is investigated. The thread produced by dry spinning of the CNTs synthesized by a floating catalyst CVD method was treated with a magnetic field in the microwave system operating at a fixed 2.45 GHz frequency. The study of the structure and elemental composition of the pristine CNT thread and the CNT threads subjected to a 1.3 kW microwave magnetic field is provided. An explanation of the paramagnetic behavior of CNT threads and an analysis of the interaction of threads with microwave radiation are presented.

articleTitle: Study on the Antibacterial Effect Based on ZIF-8@RF@Ag Reagent
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: ZIF-8 (Zn-MOF) is a metal-organic framework prepared by the reaction of zinc ions and dimethylimidazole. It has good physical and chemical properties and has broad application prospects in the field of bacterial infection. In this study, low-cost Ag@RF@ZIF-8 (ZRA) was developed by a one-pot method with high antibacterial capacity. Ag@RF@ZIF-8 nanocomposits were successfully prepared and further proved by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), ultraviolet visible (UV-vis) spectroscopy, and Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy. In vitro antibacterial experiments showed that Ag@RF@ZIF-8 had a strong antibacterial activity against E.coli and S.aureus. Therefore, the low-cost e has potential application in bacterial infections.

articleTitle: A Highly Compatible and Step-by-step Temporary Bonding and Debonding Strategy for Ultra-thin Wafer Level Package
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: With the increasing demands for lightweight, low- power, multifunctional and high-performance electronic device, such as power devices, intelligent sensors, memories and quantum devices, it has become increasingly difficult to manufacture high-performance chips solely by reducing process dimensions to meet the future development needs of integrated semiconductor devices. Over the past decades, wafer level package has been demonstrated to overcome the limitations of Moore’s Law in the physical expansion of chip manufacturing processes through three-dimension vertical interconnection technology and thin wafer processing. Temporary bonding and debonding, as a novel wafer level package technology, can provide necessary mechanical support for large-scale wafer’s three-dimension stacking and back thinning. In this paper, we proposed a highly compatible and step-by-step temporary bonding and debonding strategy. The wafer was bonded to the carrier via polymer adhesive through thermal compression bonding. The front of wafer was debonded by thermal sliding, and the back was debonded by ultraviolet laser irradiation. This strategy offers a wide process window which can be compatible with wafer process conditions such as back thinning, ion implantation, metal deposition, laser annealing and flip chip interconnection. The packaged device using this step-by-step temporary bonding and debonding technology shows an average yield of over 90%.

articleTitle: Development of a Micromanipulator Robot for Cell Injection with Sub-picoliter Scale
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This paper presents a micromanipulator robot system for cell injection with sub-picoliter scale, which is mainly composed of visual module, precision positioning module, cell holding module, cell injection module and control module. In this system, the cell manipulation is guided via visual feedback algorithm, which makes the cell injection automatically. Cell holding module and cell injection module are used to hold and inject cells, both of which are realized by a pneumatic syringebased pump, respectively. A dual-loop controller based on PID and integrated sliding-mode algorithm is used in the pump to regulate the liquid injected into the cell. As for the cell holding module, a switch control method is utilized to adjust the module keeping holding/releasing state. The precision positioning module produces high precision displacement via the step motor and lead screw nut, which is able to realize a resolution of sub-micrometer. Finally, the prototype of the proposed robot system is fabricated. The experimental studies validate that the robot system is feasible and high performance.

articleTitle: Manipulation of Zincum Oxide Nanowires for Bionanosensors Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The individual ZnO nanowires are recognized recently as promising highly sensitive media for the gas and bionanosensors in configuration of properly functionalized field-effect-transistor (NWFET). The aim of the present work is to create an experimental prototype of ZnO NWFET using mechanical bottom-up 3D nanomanipulation by shape memory nanotweezers thermally controlled in the vacuum chamber of SEM.The nanotweezers were used to create NWFETs as well as FIB-CVD. The ZnO nanowire width was from 15 to 300 nm. The length of ZnO nanowires was in the range of 1 to 50 μm.

articleTitle: Si Nanowires-holes Arrays with Enhanced Wettability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Surface engineering has made substantial advances in recent years, owing to the demand for increased wetting qualities in a variety of applications. In this study, we describe a novel method for improving surface wettability by developing nanostructured silicon nanowires-holes Si (NWs-NHs) arrays. Two-beam laser interference lithography (LIL) was used to make patterns, and metal-assisted chemical etching (MACE) was used to produce Si (NWs-NHs) arrays. The development of hydrophobic Si nanostructures, which exhibit a higher hydrophobicity than bare Si, also increased the surface wettability. Using a scanning electron microscope (SEM), the surface shape and chemical composition of the created nanostructures were examined. Measurements of the contact angles were used to describe the wettability properties. This study exemplifies the potential of LIL and MACE approaches for the creation of Si nanostructures with distinctive features, which have applications in self-cleaning surfaces, anti-fog coatings, microfluidic devices, and air humidity control.

articleTitle: Conjugation Electro-spinning Toward Janus-like Micro-fibers Array Displaying Magnetic-blue Fluorescent-conductive Aeolotropism
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Herein, a peculiar anisotropic conductive film with superior multifunction is developed. Conjugation electro-spinning fabricated Janus-like micro-fibers array (CJMA) is manufactured with $\left[\mathrm{CoFe}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4} / \mathrm{CBS}-127 / \mathrm{PMMA}\right] /[\mathrm{CB} / \mathrm{PMMA}]$ Janus-like micro-fiber as building block. The rational utilization of conjugation electro-spinning to build Janus-like micro-fibers can shun diffusion phenomena between two spinning dopes in the manufacturing process via bi-axis parallel electro-spinning, and restrict the functional fillings to their own zones to avoid infaust mutual impacts. Microscopically, the separation of conductive fillings from insulating fluorescent and magnetic fillings is completely achieved in Janus-like micro-fiber. Therefore, the insulative region of Janus-like micro-fiber has excellent fluorescent, magnetic and high insulative properties, and the conductive region has strong electrical conductivity. Macroscopically, CJMA has blue fluorescence, magnetism and strong aeolotropic conduction. The unique design idea supplies technical guidance and strategy for the fabrication of multi-functionalized anisotropic conductive films.

articleTitle: Laser-induced Fluorescence Detection of Cold-induced RNA Binding Protein Based on the Fluorescence Enhancement Effect of Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Fluorescence immunoassay technology assumes a pivotal role in achieving exceptional sensitivity for disease biomarker detection. In this paper, we proposed a cost-effective and user-friendly fluorescence biosensing method with a low detection limit for the detection of liver cancer. We fabricated fluorescence immunosensors by 300-nm SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> photonic crystal films through vertical deposition. Our method utilized the fluorescence enhancement effect in conjunction with laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) detection technology. Based on the comprehensive analysis of simulation and experimental results, we concluded that the optimal fluorescence enhancement effect of the fabricated film occurs when the incident angle is set to 45°, corresponding to an emission wavelength of 520 nm. The immunosensor exhibited a linear correlation between the fluorescence intensity and the cold-induced RNA binding protein (CIRP) concentration in the range of 0.01 ng/mL to 1000 ng/mL, with a detection limit of 0.01 ng/mL. Moreover, the immunosensor can be tuned to detect other proteins of interest depending on the immobilized antibody.

articleTitle: Droplet-based Microfluidic Platform for High-throughput Formation of Multicellular Spheroids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Cell culture in vitro is essential for drug screening, disease modeling, and stem cell-related research. Previous studies have indicated that two-dimensional (2D) cellular environments can significantly differ from physiological cells in vivo, leading to a high failure rate when translating therapeutics developed in 2D cell models to clinical applications. Therefore, there is a strong focus on developing three-dimensional (3D) cell culture techniques that more closely mimic in vivo cell microenvironments. These techniques hold great promise for enhancing precision in drug discovery and tissue regeneration. In this study, we introduce a novel microfluidic technique that utilizes droplets to fabricate hydrogel microspheres, each exhibiting a unique internal morphology suitable for 3D cell culture applications. Specifically, we employed this method to cultivate human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) within the interior canals of the hydrogel microspheres, forming monolayers on the surfaces of the spiral canals. This setup effectively mimicked the configurations of native blood vessels. Furthermore, we successfully demonstrated the fabrication of heterogeneous spheroids with spiral blood vessel lumens, which can be utilized to construct spiral vascularized bone tissue.

articleTitle: Optical Super-resolution Diagnostics: A Review of Sub-wavelength Measurements and Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Optical super-resolution diagnostics have revolutionised the field of imaging by visualising structures beyond the previously established diffraction and information resolution limits established by [1] –[3]. They have enabled the visualisation of structures at the nanoscale, changing the field of microscopic imaging for a variety of fields, including biomedical imaging, material science and nanotechnology. This paper presents an overview of several current super-resolution diagnostic techniques, describing the different optical limitations and resolutions as well as a discussion of the new knowledge that can be unlocked by the application of these technologies in areas of material and biomedical science.

articleTitle: Tribological Behavior of Medium Molecular Weight Chitosan in Acid Aqueous Solution
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Natural biomacromolecules are widely used in biomimetic medicine engineering. Especially, polysaccharides have been extensively exploited in biomedical applications due to featuring desirable lower toxicity, biocompatibility, and degradability. Chitosan, as a typical natural polysaccharide, was widely utilized as a potential vector for gene/drug delivery according to its adhesion. However, it usually coexists with tribological behaviors in these application scenarios. Many studies have explored its adhesion properties, but the tribological behavior is not clear between the two chitosan-coated surfaces. Here, we investigated the tribological behavior of chitosan films by virtue of the surface forces apparatus (SFA) under shearing in 150 mM acetic acid. The thickness of chitosan films was observed, which would gradually increase and become stable once the two chitosan films under sliding, and the variation of the chitosan thickness is reversible. It could be attributed to the generation of a hemifusion layer at the bearingload area under the high load, and the new contact interfaces were generated when relative sliding occurred. Meanwhile, the configuration of chitosan films would be rearranged with elastic swelling deformation during a running-in stage. Interestingly, the kinetic friction exhibited a negative correlation with load, in which increasing the load would result in a decrease of friction force. Such phenomenon is primarily attributed to form a more compact configuration of the new contact interfaces with a higher charge density, which reduced the opportunities for the polymer interpenetration of entanglement of the chitosan chains and enhanced the electrostatic repulsion between the new contact interfaces, leading to smaller friction. Our findings provide useful information in understanding the tribology mechanism of soft materials, with implications onto designing chitosan-based lubricating materials for biomedical and bioengineering.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Discharge Process in Electrical Discharge Machining of NiTi Shape Memory Alloys
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: The material is removed by thermal effect by wire electrical discharge machining (WEDM) and a thermal damage layer is formed on the machined surface, which affects the function and performance of NiTi shape memory alloys (NiTiSMAs). However, the material removal process and thermal damage of WEDM are not clear. Therefore, by establishing the empirical formula of discharge channel radius, and based on the theory of heat transfer field and fluid mechanics, the finite element mode of crater morphology evolution and material removal process of WEDM is established in this paper. The results show that the reaction force of the vaporized metal and the gradient of surface tension caused by temperature are the fundamental reasons for driving the molten flow in the pit to both sides and forming bulges. The spatter of molten material is caused by the reaction force of metal vapor greater than the surface tension. When the material absorbs and transfers heat at a rate close to the same level during removal, a steady state effect will be formed, so that the recast layer changes within a certain range. Under the same machining conditions, the simulation and experimental results agree well with the geometry of the dent. The error of the crater depth is 14.6 %, while the error of the crater diameter is only 5.8 %. Therefore, the established model can provide insights into the material removal and thermal damage formation of NiTi-SMAs machined by WEDM

articleTitle: Swarm Robot SLAM with Point-Line Matching in Weak Information Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) in weak information environment scenarios where there are only sparse and ambiguous references are available presents significant challenges. This paper introduces a swarm robots based point-line matching based solution to enhance the accuracy and robustness of localization and mapping within such environments. Our approach employs a centralized serverbased architecture for the swarm robot system and utilizes an ORB-based Distributed Bag-of-Words (DBoW) algorithm to construct point and line feature dictionaries. By generating point-line pairs, the proposed method effectively addresses perceptual overlap issues, thereby improving the overall performance of localization and mapping for swarm robots. Experimental results validate the superiority of the proposed approach in comparison to traditional methods, highlighting its potential for real-world applications in challenging environments for swarm robot SLAM.

articleTitle: Monitoring Method of Acoustic Emission Technology for Micro Texture of PCD Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: This research investigates the potential of employing nanosecond lasers to achieve micro-hole texturing on the frontal surface of polycrystalline diamond (PCD) tools. A sequence of experiments, each focusing on an individual factor, was executed to explore the effects of varying laser pulse energies on the dimensions of micro-holes and the scope of the recast layer. Concurrently, real-time acoustic emission (AE) signals, produced during the texturing procedure, were gathered and subjected to analysis using characteristic AE parameters and the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) based on waveforms. The association between texturing patterns and AE signals was subsequently established. The findings unveil that as laser energy intensffies, both the diameter of micro-holes and the extent of the recast layer increase proportionally. Furthermore, the amplitude, MARSE (Measured Area under the Rectified Signal Envelope), and spectral analysis of AE signals effectively depict the structural attributes of the textured surface. These results underscore a profound connection between AE signals and the structural traits of micro-textured surfaces.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Techniques For AFM-Based Imaging of Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: In recent years, advances in computer vision and machine learning have supported a series of algorithms, and their ability to decipher image contents is impressive. These algorithms are being applied to the study of cell images, and gradually changing the analysis methods of cell image data. Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) is a powerful tool for imaging and analyzing cell structures. It has been used to study the morphology, structure and mechanical properties of cells. However, it is still a challenging topic to identify cells based on AFM images. This article summarizes the applications of machine learning methods in the cell image analysis by AFM. The research of the cell analysis method begins with the collection of cell data, and it emphasizes to identifying cell types, carcinogenesis or carcinogenesis levels, and its auxiliary work includes the cell segmentation, denoising, super-resolution, generation and simulation. Finally, the research experience in these analysis methods and their guiding significance for further study are discussed.

articleTitle: Body Fluid Identification by Nanoparticle Enhanced LDI MS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Body fluids contain valuable information about human body and are the most significant evidence in forensic investigation at crime scenes. Their characterizations can provide investigative leads and contributes to case proof. Identifying different kinds of body fluids is critical but challenging. Traditional forensic methods rely on enzymatic assays as presumptive tests, which are destructive and invasive to samples, as well as time-consuming and complex in procedures, resulting in their inability to meet the demand of rapid detection. Here, a body fluids (including serum, plasma, tear, and urine) integrated identification platform through machine learning of metabolic fingerprinting (MF) was developed, using nanoparticle enhanced laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (NPELDI MS). The direct MFs of multiplex body fluids were acquired with fast speed (10 s per sample) and high reproducibility (coefficient of variation, CV < 15%) at sample volume of 5 nL, coexisting with minimum sample invasiveness. Further, two strategies (four classifications and dichotomy) were conducted to identify diverse body fluids through machine learning with the area under the cures (AUCs) of 0.969 for four classifications and 0.973 to 1.000 for dichotomy, respectively. Finally, a biomarker panel was established, and it improved the performance of body fluids identification with AUC of 1.000. Our work provides a frontier reference for differentiating body fluids through metabolomics and innovative perspectives for forensic application.

articleTitle: Single-molecule Electrical Characterization On A Controllable-break-junction Chip through Electrostatic Microactuators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Molecular electronics endeavors to create extensive integrated circuits by linking and managing individual molecules as electronic components, presenting a novel avenue for the exploration of future ultra-compact electronic devices. Currently, this field mainly uses dynamic break junction technology to build single-molecule junctions with high success rates and stability and to investigate the electronic properties of the single-molecular. However, the existing break junction technology still faces challenges in attaining manageable preparation and integrated connection of single-molecular electronic devices, due to the complexity of instrumentation. This work presents the development of a chip-integrated single-molecule break junction system utilizing micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) technology. The system includes an electrostatic actuator and an in-plane suspended golden bridge, which is driven by an electrostatic comb actuator to perform tapping mode for building single-molecule junctions. By assembling the molecules to the chip, we achieved single-molecule conductance detection of 1,6-hexanedithiol, confirming that the device can be used for single-molecule break junction experiments. This device greatly simplifies traditional single-molecule break junction instruments, which shows the potential to integrate single-molecule electronic devices onto chips.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Classification for AFM Images of Cancer Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Manipulation, Manufacturing and Measurement on the Nanoscale (3M-NANO)
abstract: Deep learning has exhibited promising outcomes particularly in computer vision. In the medical field, deep learning has been successfully utilized to improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in cancer diagnosis. Given the complexity of cancer, early detection and diagnosis remain challenging tasks. Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) has been reported as an important tool for the diagnosis of both benign and malignant cells, due to its ability to provide information on cell mechanics and ultrastructures. Therefore, it is meaningful to use deep learning algorithms to classify cancer cells based on AFM images. This classification can include identifying cancer subtypes and differentiatoins between benign and malignant properties. The purpose of this work is to review the progress and research implications in the area of deep learning based classification for AFM images of cancer cells.
